result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.bellman_ford_shortest_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find shortest path using Bellman-Ford algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17301-L17482){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.bellman_ford_shortest_path( source, target, attr_name=None, return_list=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes the shortest weighted path from source to target using the Bellman-Ford algorithm. Unlike Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman-Ford can handle negative edge weights and will detect negative weight cycles. Can return the path as a list, or store the position of each node along the path as a node attribute for visualization. The Bellman-Ford algorithm is slower than Dijkstra (O(VE) vs O(E log V)) but more versatile. Use it when: - the graph has negative edge weights - the graph is sparse, with few edges - you need to detect negative cycles ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node (integer ID or string label). [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target node (integer ID or string label). [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store path position. If `None`, uses `bellman_ford_path_order` as the attribute name. Position is 0-indexed (source = 0, next node = 1, ..., target = n-1). Only nodes on the path get this attribute set. [return_list]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns list of node IDs in the path. If `False`, stores positions as node attributes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[list[int], Graph, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_list=` is `True`: list of node IDs from source to target (inclusive), or `None` if no path exists. If `return_list=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining, or `None` if no path exists. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph contains a negative weight cycle. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} **Algorithm complexity:** - time: `O(V × E)` where `V` is vertices, `E` is edges - space: `O(V)` for distance and predecessor arrays - slower than Dijkstra but handles negative weights **When to use:** - graph has negative edge weights (debt, cost reductions) - graph is sparse (few edges relative to nodes) - you need to detect negative cycles (arbitrage opportunities) **Applications:** - financial modeling (debt, arbitrage detection) - network routing with cost penalties - game theory (negative payoffs) - resource allocation with penalties ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find shortest path with negative weights: ::: {#85e03706 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=4.0) .add_edge("A", "C", weight=2.0) .add_edge("C", "B", weight=-3.0) # Negative weight .add_edge("B", "D", weight=1.0) ) path = graph.bellman_ford_shortest_path("A", "D", return_list=True) # Path: A -> C -> B -> D (takes negative weight edge) # Returns [1, 3, 2, 4] (node IDs) path ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 3, 2, 4] ``` ::: ::: Store path as node attributes for visualization: ::: {#cc597c29 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=4.0) .add_edge("A", "C", weight=2.0) .add_edge("C", "B", weight=-3.0) .add_edge("B", "D", weight=1.0) .bellman_ford_shortest_path("A", "D", return_list=False) .colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from="bellman_ford_path_order", palette="plasma" ) ) graph.get_node_attrs("bellman_ford_path_order") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {3: 1, 1: 0, 4: 3, 2: 2} ``` ::: ::: Detect negative cycle: ::: {#724eb735 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} bad_graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.0) .add_edge("B", "C", weight=-3.0) .add_edge("C", "A", weight=1.0) # Creates negative cycle ) error_message = None try: bad_graph.bellman_ford_shortest_path("A", "B", return_list=True) except ValueError as e: error_message = str(e) error_message ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 'Graph contains a negative weight cycle' ``` ::: ::: Handle unreachable target: ::: {#73924004 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="isolated") result = graph.bellman_ford_shortest_path("A", "isolated", return_list=True) # Returns None (no path exists) result ``` :::
